title: agentHost: preserve legacy Copilot CLI session titles on migration
body:
## Problem
Migrated legacy Copilot CLI sessions lose their title and show the default "Session", even though they had a meaningful title before migration.

## Root cause
Adoption (`ensureChatAdopted`) carried only the VS Code `customTitle` marker — a staging field written only before a session's SDK session exists. For 'normal' sessions the real title lives in the SDK `name` (`workspace.yaml`), with `summary` as a secondary source. Adoption never read either, so sessions without a staged `customTitle` migrated with no title.

## Fix
Carry the title with a fallback chain matching the extension's own resolution:
`customTitle ?? sdkMetadata.name ?? sdkMetadata.summary`. Additive — `customTitle`
still wins when present; only the missing `name`/`summary` fallback is added (`sdkMetadata` is already fetched during adoption).

## Tests
New tests for the `name` fallback (proving it beats `summary`) and the `summary`
fallback; the existing custom-title test is unchanged.

title: Optimize repeated unit test startup
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #333137 and [review feedback](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/333137#pullrequestreview-5050500099).

- check the cached Electron version and expected executable directly in the unit-test launchers
- avoid starting the TypeScript prelaunch helper on every cached test run
- invalidate the cache when Electron changes or the executable is renamed
- use `npm run electron` as the cache-miss entry point on Windows and Unix
- support `VSCODE_FORCE_PRELAUNCH=1` for packaging changes that require forced repackaging
- preserve the existing expectation that dependencies are installed before invoking the test launchers

## Validation

- focused chat Find unit tests: 30 passing with the cached Electron timestamp unchanged
- no `DEP0180` / `fs.Stats` warning on the cached run
- cached validation benchmark: ~2.4 ms versus ~189 ms for launching the TypeScript prelaunch helper
- verified the package script maps to `node build/lib/electron.ts` and no gulp `electron` task exists
- `npm --prefix build run typecheck`
- `git diff --check`

title: agentHost: observe dispatched actions through a chat contribution hook
body:
agentHost: observe dispatched actions through a chat contribution hook

Moves session input-needed aggregation, turn-usage persistence, and session flag persistence
out of `AgentSideEffects`, which loses 252 lines, and closes the last gaps where a turn ended
without telling contributions.

## Dispatched-action hook

All three moved behaviors observed `AgentHostStateManager.onDidEmitEnvelope` rather than the
client dispatch path, so none could use the existing action hook: most of the actions they
react to are dispatched by the host, not by a client.

- Adds `onDidDispatchAction`, which observes an action from any origin once its outcome is
  known, including server-dispatched actions and rejected ones that never reduced. It is a
  separate hook and not a widening of the client hook, because `queueDrain` depends on that
  hook being client-only and would otherwise see each client action twice.
- Adds `SessionInputNeededContribution` (order 200), which mirrors per-chat blockers into the
  owning session's `inputNeeded` list. This is the bulk of the move at roughly 170 lines.
- Gives `PersistedTurnUsageContribution` the write half of turn-usage persistence. It already
  owned the restore half, so one contribution now owns both directions, as chat drafts and
  chat titles already do.
- Adds `SessionFlagsContribution` (order 700) for read state, archived state, and merged
  config values. It preserves an asymmetry that is easy to lose: read and archived changes
  skip a rejected action, config values do not.
- Makes `AgentHostToolCallTracker` injectable. Input-needed reports blocked and unblocked tool
  calls to it, and it was constructed inside `AgentSideEffects`, so a contribution could not
  reach it.

## Terminal turn outcomes

A turn that captured a start checkpoint and then failed to send never scheduled its changeset
recompute, because `captureTurnStartCheckpoint` runs before `sendMessage` but the catch never
reported the end.

- Reports a turn end when a send throws, which fixes that bug.
- Reports a turn end for a client-dispatched cancellation, which the agent-signal path already
  did. This fires exactly once: the reducer clears the active turn first, so a later
  agent-emitted cancellation takes the no-active-turn path, which reports only completions.
- Adds a `rejected` reason for requests refused before their turn started, fired from both
  `startTurn` early returns.
- Makes `MarkUnreadContribution` ignore `rejected`. It filtered negatively, so a rejection on
  an archived session would have marked it unread and resurfaced it.
- Leaves `QueueDrainContribution` untouched for `rejected`. A rejected queued turn consumes
  its message and the queue stalls, but draining would cascade an archived chat through every
  queued message. The fix is to return the message to the queue, which is recorded as such.

## Naming

Renames the two action hooks so each says what it observes:

- `onAction` becomes `onDidApplyClientAction`, and `IObservedAction` becomes
  `IAppliedClientAction`. Rejected client actions never reach it, so an action it sees always
  reduced.
- `onEnvelope` becomes `onDidDispatchAction`, and `IObservedEnvelope` becomes
  `IDispatchedAction`. It also delivers rejected actions, so a name claiming they were applied
  would be wrong.

## Tests and docs

Registers the built-in contributions in the tool-call and turn-hang telemetry test graphs.
Both build `AgentSideEffects` without them, so they stopped exercising blocked-call telemetry
once that reporting moved into a contribution. The graphs now mirror production wiring; no
assertion changed. Both new `agentSideEffects` tests were confirmed to fail without the
turn-end fix.

Updates the contributions skill, which described four hooks and named two that no longer
exist. It now documents all seven, records that the admission hook fails closed and is
synchronous while every other hook isolates failures, and carries the design rationale that
`TODO.md` used to hold. `TODO.md` keeps only open work and caveats, with each fact in one
place.

title: fix: clamp inverted visible range in ListView to prevent RangeError (fixes #333230)
body:
### Summary `RangeError: Invalid array length` is thrown in `ListView.probeDynamicHeights` (`src/vs/base/browser/ui/list/listView.ts`) when it evaluates `new Array(range.end - range.start)` with an **inverted range** (`end < start`). The negative length throws immediately. The inverted range originates in `getVisibleRange(renderTop, renderHeight)`. When the viewport is collapsed or hidden during a layout pass (`renderHeight <= 0`), the expression `renderTop + renderHeight - 1` becomes smaller than `renderTop`. Because `rangeMap.indexAfter(position) = min(indexAt(position) + 1, count)` is monotonic in `position`, the resulting `end` can resolve to an index **before** `start`, yielding `{ start, end }` with `end < start`. This malformed `IRange` violates the `start <= end` invariant that consumers assume. This is a recent regression (new bucket in 1.135.0, 411 users): the previous `_rerender` iterated with `for (let i = range.start; i < range.end; i++)`, which silently tolerated an inverted range by not iterating. The batched-measurement rewrite replaced that loop with an eagerly-sized array, turning the previously-harmless inverted range into a hard crash. Fixes microsoft/vscode#333230 Recommended reviewer: `@connor4312` ### Culprit Commit `c2b336daae7101676f179b30f92641cdfcc6b38c` — "list: batch dynamic height measurements (#330967)" by Connor Peet (`connor4312`), 2026-08-18. This commit falls within the reported regression range (`0d0c8a6...68161d9`, 1.134.0-insider → 1.135.0-insider) and introduced `probeDynamicHeights`, which allocates `new Array(range.end - range.start)` without guaranteeing `end >= start`. ### Code Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[layout / setScrollDimensions with renderHeight <= 0] --> B[onScroll] B --> C[_rerender] C --> D["getVisibleRange(renderTop, renderHeight)"] D --> E["end = indexAfter(renderTop + renderHeight - 1)
can be < start when renderHeight ≤ 0"] E --> F["inverted IRange: end < start"] F --> G["probeDynamicHeights(range)"] G --> H["new Array(range.end - range.start)
negative length"] H --> I["RangeError: Invalid array length"] ``` ### Affected Files - `src/vs/base/browser/ui/list/listView.ts` — `getVisibleRange` (producer of the inverted range) and `probeDynamicHeights` (crash site). ### Repro Steps Not reliably reproducible via manual steps; occurs under a layout race. Conceptually: 1. Host a `ListView` inside a widget whose container can be laid out with zero/negative height (e.g., a collapsed chat/inline-chat widget). 2. Trigger a layout/scroll pass while `renderHeight <= 0`. 3. `getVisibleRange` returns an inverted range; `probeDynamicHeights` allocates a negative-length array and throws `RangeError: Invalid array length`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/base/browser/ui/list/listView.ts`, `getVisibleRange`: compute `start` first, then clamp `end` with `Math.max(start, indexAfter(renderTop + renderHeight - 1))`. This fixes the bug at the data producer rather than at the crash site: `getVisibleRange` constructs the `IRange`, so enforcing the `start <= end` invariant there guarantees every consumer (including `probeDynamicHeights`) receives a well-formed range. An empty range (`start === end`) is valid and yields a zero-length array, restoring the harmless behavior the previous `for`-loop had. After this change, `getVisibleRange` cannot produce a range with `end < start` because `end` is explicitly clamped to be at least `start`, so `range.end - range.start` is always `>= 0` and `new Array(...)` can no longer receive a negative length. **Alternatives considered:** - Guard at the crash site in `probeDynamicHeights` (e.g., early-return or clamp the array length there) — rejected because it patches the symptom at the bottom of the stack while leaving the malformed `IRange` flowing to every other consumer; the fix must live where the invalid data is produced. ### Recommended Owner `connor4312` (Connor Peet) — authored the culprit commit `c2b336daae71` and is an active repository collaborator with recent commits. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/33202685801) · opus48 · 452.1 AIC · ⌖ 11.3 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)

title: fix: revive telemetryInfo.sessionResource on chat editing timeline restore (fixes #333229)
body:
### Summary `isAgentHostSessionResource(this._telemetryInfo.sessionResource)` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'scheme')` because `sessionResource` is `undefined`, violating its non-nullable `readonly sessionResource: URI` contract. The invalid value originates when a chat editing session's **checkpoint timeline** is persisted and restored: the telemetry info objects are getter-backed anonymous class instances, and `JSON.stringify` drops their prototype getters, so the restored objects lack `sessionResource`. The snapshot restore path already re-injects the session resource, but the timeline restore path did not. This fix re-injects the owning `chatSessionResource` into timeline-restored telemetry info, mirroring the snapshot path. Fixes microsoft/vscode#333229 Recommended reviewer: `@connor4312` ### Culprit Commit `8f4fc8d3273653bfb73b8d4c3cfc7eeecd00722c` — "chat: identify Agent Host telemetry sessions (#332000)" by Connor Peet (copeet@microsoft.com), Aug 21 2026. This commit introduced the `isAgentHostSessionResource(this._telemetryInfo.sessionResource)` call in `chatEditingModifiedFileEntry.ts`, which newly dereferences `.scheme` on a `sessionResource` that can be `undefined` after a timeline restore. Shipped in commit `08d4889f9ec4a1685d257b9b95de036c8e1ce1e5` (Version 1.135.0, last seen Aug 27 2026); the culprit (Aug 21) is an ancestor of the shipped build (Aug 27). ### Code Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[_getTelemetryInfoForModel
chatEditingSession.ts:1030] -->|anonymous class
getter-based sessionResource| B[telemetryInfo on operations & fileBaselines] B --> C[getStateForPersistence
chatEditingCheckpointTimelineImpl.ts] C -->|JSON.stringify drops
prototype getters| D[persisted timeline state
sessionResource lost] D --> E[restoreFromState
operations/baselines rehydrated
sessionResource = undefined] E --> F[_notifyAction
chatEditingModifiedFileEntry.ts:277] F --> G[isAgentHostSessionResource
chatSessionsService.ts:405] G -->|resource.scheme| H[TypeError: reading 'scheme'] ``` ### Affected Files - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatEditing/chatEditingCheckpointTimelineImpl.ts` — timeline restore path; the fix re-injects `sessionResource` here. - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatEditing/chatEditingModifiedFileEntry.ts` (crash site, line 277) — unchanged; not the correct fix location. - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatSessionsService.ts` (line 405, throw site) — unchanged. - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatEditing/chatEditingSession.ts` (line 1030, producer of getter-based telemetry info) — unchanged. ### Repro Steps 1. Start a chat editing session that produces file operations/baselines (edits with an agent). 2. Persist the session so its checkpoint timeline state is serialized via `JSON.stringify`. 3. Reload the window so the timeline is restored via `restoreFromState`; the restored `telemetryInfo.sessionResource` is `undefined` because the getter was dropped during serialization. 4. Trigger a session action (`_notifyAction`), which calls `isAgentHostSessionResource(this._telemetryInfo.sessionResource)` → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'scheme')`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`chatEditingCheckpointTimelineImpl.ts`): In `restoreFromState`, restored `operations` (Create ops) and `fileBaselines` now pass their `telemetryInfo` through a new `_reviveTelemetryInfo` helper that re-injects the timeline's own `chatSessionResource` when `sessionResource` is missing. This fixes the data at the restore boundary — the actual producer of the invalid value — rather than guarding the crash site. The bypass is the `JSON.stringify` round-trip that silently drops the getter-backed `sessionResource` (declared non-nullable `URI`), and the restore boundary is where the type contract must be re-established. This mirrors the existing snapshot restore path, which already re-injects `this._chatSessionResource`. After this change, `restoreFromState` cannot yield a `telemetryInfo` with an undefined `sessionResource`, because every restored operation/baseline telemetry info is passed through `_reviveTelemetryInfo`, which substitutes the timeline's `chatSessionResource` whenever the deserialized value is missing. **Alternatives considered:** - Add `?.` / a guard at the crash site (`chatEditingModifiedFileEntry.ts:277`) — rejected because it masks the symptom at the consumer instead of fixing the data producer, leaving `sessionResource` `undefined` for every other consumer and violating the non-nullable contract silently. - Change the producer `_getTelemetryInfoForModel` to use own enumerable properties instead of getters — rejected because the getters are intentional (the response result is not available when editing starts), and it would not repair already-persisted state. ### Recommended Owner `@connor4312` (Connor Peet) — author of the culprit commit `8f4fc8d3`, active collaborator (recent commit Aug 27 2026), and owner of the Agent Host telemetry session code. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/33202683766) · opus48 · 623.6 AIC · ⌖ 12 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)

title: fix: fall back to in-process diff when worker creation fails (fixes #333223)
body:
### Summary `new Worker(...)` throws `EINVAL` when the copilot-chat extension host tries to spin up the diff worker thread on some win32 machines (worker threads unavailable/blocked). `DiffServiceImpl` caches this construction error in a `Lazy`, so every subsequent `computeDiff` call permanently rejects even though an identical in-process diff implementation already ships. The rejection escapes through the edit-survival telemetry path (`stringEditFromDiff` → `EditCollector.getEdits` → `startReporter`'s un-`catch`ed async IIFE) as an unhandled error, affecting 24 users on 0.62.0. Fixes microsoft/vscode#333223 Recommended reviewer: `@chrmarti` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`3b795b1e583`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/3b795b1e58326cf6c70a7d39270981ce2c885128) | | Author | `@chrmarti` | | PR | #807 | | Message | Extract `@vscode/chat-lib` (#807) | | Why | This commit introduced the `_useWorker` split in `DiffServiceImpl.computeDiff` (lines 46-48), routing diffs through `this._worker.value.proxy.computeDiff`. When `new Worker` throws `EINVAL`, the `Lazy` caches the error and the worker branch re-throws on every call, with no fallback to the already-present in-process branch — turning an environmental worker-thread failure into a permanent, unhandled rejection. This is an ancestor of the shipped commit `08d4889`. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Reporter as EditSurvivalTrackerService.startReporter participant Collector as EditCollector.getEdits participant Edit as stringEditFromDiff participant Diff as DiffServiceImpl.computeDiff participant Lazy as Lazy participant Worker as new Worker Reporter->>Collector: getEdits() Collector->>Edit: stringEditFromDiff(...) Edit->>Diff: computeDiff(original, modified, opts) Note over Diff: ⚠️ Root cause:
worker branch with no fallback Diff->>Lazy: this._worker.value Lazy->>Worker: new Worker(workerPath) Note over Worker: 💥 EINVAL thrown
(worker threads unavailable) Worker-->>Reporter: unhandled rejection (no catch in startReporter IIFE) ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `extensions/copilot/src/util/node/worker.ts` | crash site | L90: `this.worker = new Worker(workerPath, workerOptions)` throws EINVAL | | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/diff/node/diffServiceImpl.ts` | root cause | L46-48: `this._useWorker ? await this._worker.value.proxy.computeDiff(...) : await diffWorker.computeDiff(...)` — worker branch has no fallback when construction fails | | `extensions/copilot/src/util/vs/base/common/lazy.ts` | error amplifier | L37-50: caches the executor error and re-throws it on every `.value` access | | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/editSurvivalTracking/common/editSurvivalTrackerService.ts` | escape path | L62-70: `startReporter` async IIFE has `try/finally` but no `catch`, so the diff rejection becomes an unhandled error | ### Repro Steps 1. Run VS Code + copilot-chat 0.62.0 on a win32 environment where `worker_threads` construction fails (`new Worker` throws `EINVAL`, e.g. constrained/locked-down hosts). 2. Trigger an AI edit so edit-survival tracking starts (`startReporter`), which calls `EditCollector.getEdits()` → `stringEditFromDiff` → `DiffServiceImpl.computeDiff`. 3. The first `computeDiff` constructs the `Lazy` worker; `new Worker` throws `EINVAL`, the error is cached, and the promise rejects. 4. Because the `startReporter` IIFE has no `catch`, the rejection surfaces as `unhandlederror-EINVAL`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`extensions/copilot/src/platform/diff/node/diffServiceImpl.ts` → `computeDiff()`): resolve the lazy worker inside a `try/catch` in `computeDiff`. If worker construction throws (e.g. `EINVAL`), disable the worker (`this._useWorker = false`) and fall back to the in-process `diffWorker.computeDiff`, which produces identical results (both branches call the same `computeDiffSync` logic). This is a data-producer fix: the diff service is the producer of the rejected promise, and the worker is only a performance optimization with an already-shipping in-process equivalent. The `catch` is scoped strictly to worker *construction* (`this._worker.value`) — actual diff-computation errors from `worker.proxy.computeDiff` still propagate, so no genuine error is swallowed and no `logService.error` call is removed. **Alternatives considered**: - Add a `catch` to the `startReporter` async IIFE that logs via `logService.error`. Rejected: that only silences the symptom at the consumer/escape path and would leave the diff service permanently broken for every other consumer once the worker fails to construct, degrading all diff-dependent functionality instead of transparently falling back. - Guard `new Worker` inside `worker.ts`. Rejected: `WorkerWithRpcProxy` is a generic RPC primitive; swallowing construction failures there would hide real misconfiguration from other callers, whereas `DiffServiceImpl` is the specific consumer that has a correct in-process fallback. ### Recommended Owner `@chrmarti` — author of culprit commit #807, which introduced the `_useWorker` worker/in-process split in `DiffServiceImpl`; core VS Code maintainer with recent activity. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/33201025964) · opus48 · 425.9 AIC · ⌖ 11.7 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)

title: fix: defer terminal tool confirmation editor layout to next animation frame (fixes #333221)
body:
### Summary `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` is firing across the chat confirmation surface. The synthetic browser warning carries only non-causal delivery context (`ResizeObserverLoopContext(...)`) listing the wrapped observers that ran in the same rendering frame — the browser does not expose the actual observer that skipped a delivery. Among the listed observers, the one that synchronously writes layout back into its own observed element is `ChatTerminalToolConfirmationSubPart.editor`, which calls `editor.object.layout(width)` inside the resize callback; that write flexes the embedded editor's height back into the observed `elements.editor`, re-entering the same observation phase and tripping the loop warning under bursty resizes. Impact: noisy unhandled-error telemetry (spike on `1.136.0-insider`), no functional break. Fixes microsoft/vscode#333221 Recommended reviewer: `@bryanchen-d` ### Culprit Commit No single culprit commit introduced this regression. The observers named in the bucket context (`BaseChatConfirmationWidget.message`, `BaseChatConfirmationWidget.messageContent`, `ChatInputPart.containerHeight`, `ChatTerminalToolConfirmationSubPart.editor`, `ChatThinkingContentPart.wrapper`, `ChatToolConfirmationCarouselPart.contentExpansion`) all pre-date the `08d4889f...3fcbd108` regression window — a `-S` search for each name inside the range returns nothing. The `[ResizeObserverLoopContext(...)]` bucketing format itself was introduced in #328065 (Jul 29), also before the window. This is the same self-feeding pattern previously fixed for `ChatInputPart.containerHeight` in [#316524](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/316524) (fixes \#316509), recurring in a sibling widget. The spike is best explained by increased exercise of the terminal tool confirmation surface rather than a new triggering commit, so the bug is treated as pre-existing and the fix is applied at the self-feeding write site. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Browser as Browser layout participant Observer as ChatTerminalToolConfirmationSubPart.editor observer participant Editor as editor.object participant Site as elements.editor (observed) Browser->>Observer: deliver resize entry (width) Note over Observer: ⚠️ Root cause:
synchronous editor.object.layout(width) Observer->>Editor: layout(width) Editor->>Site: height flexes back into observed element Site->>Browser: resize re-entered in same phase Note over Browser: 💥 ResizeObserver loop completed
with undelivered notifications ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/toolInvocationParts/chatTerminalToolConfirmationSubPart.ts` | root cause / fix | L194-L200 (pre-fix): `new DisposableResizeObserver('ChatTerminalToolConfirmationSubPart.editor', entries => { ... editor.object.layout(width); })` — synchronous layout write into the observed element | | `src/vs/base/browser/dom.ts` | context provider | L2169-L2184: `getRecentDisposableResizeObserverContextForLoopError` — names are delivery context only, "not causal attribution" | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/chatInputPart.ts` | precedent fix | L4022-L4036: prior rAF-deferral fix for the identical pattern (#316524) | ### Repro Steps 1. Start a chat session and trigger a terminal tool confirmation so the `ChatTerminalToolConfirmationSubPart` embedded editor renders. 2. Rapidly resize the chat panel / window (or stream content that repeatedly changes the editor width) so the editor width observer fires in bursts. 3. Observe the `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` warning surface in error telemetry. It is timing-dependent; bursty width changes within a single rendering frame increase the likelihood of the browser skipping a delivery. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — In `chatTerminalToolConfirmationSubPart.ts`, the resize callback no longer calls `editor.object.layout(width)` synchronously. It records the last observed width and schedules the layout on the next animation frame via an `AnimationFrameScheduler` (disposed with the part). Deferring the layout write out of the resize-observation phase breaks the self-feeding loop while preserving the resize behavior — the editor still lays out to the observed width, just one frame later. This fixes the problem at the site that produces the feedback write (the self-resizing layout call), not at a crash site or by suppressing the warning, and it reuses the exact pattern already proven for `ChatInputPart.containerHeight` in #316524. **Alternatives considered** — Wrapping the layout call in `try/catch` was rejected because the warning is delivered as a stackless `ErrorEvent` on `window`, not thrown at the call site, so a local catch would not suppress it and would hide nothing useful. Widening or muting the telemetry context in `dom.ts` was rejected because that helper is intentionally non-causal delivery context and other observers legitimately rely on it. ### Recommended Owner `@bryanchen-d` — authored the precedent fix [#316524](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/316524) and the ResizeObserver delivery-context telemetry (#328065, #2613d4a naming), owns the chat confirmation widget area, and is the current issue assignee. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/33200593327) · opus48 · 418.4 AIC · ⌖ 12.3 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)

title: automations: add context menu actions for automation cards
body:
Adds Duplicate, Disable, and Delete actions to the automation card context menu. 

- **Duplicate** opens a prefilled Create Automation dialog with the original card's values.
- **Disable** allows users to disable an enabled automation.
- **Delete** prompts for confirmation before removing an automation.

All actions respect provider capabilities and handle concurrent changes. Accessibility guidance has been updated, and focused regression tests cover all new functionalities.

title: accounts: preserve sign-in during session replacement
body:
## Summary

- Keeps the default account signed in while GitHub authentication replaces a session in a combined event.
- Prevents the Agent Host sign-in banner from appearing during an active session when the replacement credential remains valid.
- Adds privacy-safe diagnostics that distinguish interactive-login replacements from shared secret-storage reconciliation.
- Preserves immediate sign-out behavior for removal-only events, including while replacement reconciliation is in flight.

Fixes #333197

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

GitHub Authentication can publish one session-change event containing both the removed current session and its replacement. The default-account listener treated the removal as a complete sign-out, cleared the account, and skipped reconciliation. That temporary null account propagated through chat entitlement state and caused the Agent Host sign-in banner to appear even though the replacement credential was valid.

Runtime logs from the reported occurrence show the GitHub removal and addition in the same event cycle, followed within milliseconds by the Sessions signed-out path. Subsequent authentication using the replacement credential succeeded.

### Implementation

The default-account listener now distinguishes removal-only events from events containing added or changed replacement candidates. Removal-only events still clear the account immediately. Replacement events retain the current account while the existing throttled refresh retrieves, validates, and selects the actual default session.

Each asynchronous refresh captures the current session before it starts. If that session changes while the refresh is pending, the stale result is discarded so an earlier replacement reconciliation cannot overwrite a later removal-only sign-out.

GitHub Authentication records replacement events at info level with only the source category, event kind, and added/removed/changed counts. Routine session changes remain at trace level. The logs intentionally exclude account labels and identifiers, session identifiers, scopes, and credentials.

Regression coverage drives a combined replacement and a genuine removal-only event through the authentication service fixture. A blocked-refresh case verifies that removal remains final when replacement reconciliation was already in flight.

### Behavior and constraints

- Added or changed sessions are reconciliation candidates; they are not assigned directly.
- If reconciliation finds no valid replacement, the normal refresh clears the default account.
- Events from unrelated authentication providers remain ignored.
- This change addresses the false default-account transition and sign-in banner. Remote Agent Host tunnel reconnect churn from the same authentication event remains separate follow-up work.

</details>

title: Render session artifact locations as paths and centre the artifacts file icon
body:
## Description

Artifact and reference pills in the agents window showed raw URIs (`file:///c:/Users/besimmonds/.copilot/session-state/be29001b-.../files/ab-windows.json`), and the themed file icon in the artifacts dropdown sat ~3px above the row's centre.

### Location text (`sessionArtifacts.ts`)

- `sessionArtifactLocationText` renders locations through `ILabelService.getUriLabel(uri, { relative: true })`: no scheme, tildified under the user home, native separators/drive letters (`vscode-agent-host` URIs via their registered formatter), relative to the session's folder.
- Only file-system schemes (`file`, `vscode-remote`, `vscode-userdata`, `vscode-agent-host`) become paths. Links and agent-supplied custom schemes keep their whole URI — a path label drops the scheme, authority and query, which would make them read like files that are nowhere to be found.
- A location that *is* the workspace folder has no relative label (`''`), so it falls back to its full path instead of an empty hover.
- The sections observable re-reads on `onDidChangeFormatters` and `onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders`, since the session's folder is mounted a moment after the session becomes active.

```
file:///home/alice/repo/src/app.ts   ->  src/app.ts
file:///home/alice/notes.md          ->  ~/notes.md
myapp://team/board?id=42             ->  myapp://team/board?id=42   (unchanged)
```

### Icon centring (`chatPills.css`)

- The existing rule targeted `.action-widget .action-list-item .icon.file-icon` — a class the action widget never puts on its rows — so it never applied, and the sizing sat on the wrong element (themed file icons paint through `::before`).
- Now targets `.monaco-list-row.action`, gives the icon slot the action row's height and centres the glyph inside it. Codicons are unaffected because `codicon.css` already sets `line-height: 1`; this restores the same for font- and image-based file icon themes.
- `chatDropdownPill` is the only producer of `file-icon` classes for action lists, so the newly matching selector stays scoped to chat pill dropdowns.

### Supporting

- `componentFixtures/fixtureUtils.ts` registers `IWorkspaceContextService`, needed now that `SessionArtifacts` declares it under the strict test instantiation service.
- New unit coverage for the location text; existing artifact tests pass a label service stub.

title: editor: Balance auto-closing brackets
body:
Fixes #6841

# Summary

- Keeps auto-closing brackets balanced when an opening bracket is typed before a matching unmatched closer later in the document, avoiding a duplicate closing bracket.
- Adds token- and language-aware unmatched-closer detection so brackets in strings, comments, and embedded languages do not affect the decision.

# Known Limitations

- The balancing check is skipped until token-aware bracket data is available and for documents too large for the bracket-pair AST. These cases retain the existing auto-closing behavior.
- Multi-cursor typing uses a shared auto-closing decision. If any cursor can reuse a later unmatched closer, auto-closing is suppressed for the entire edit.
- `editor.autoClosingBrackets: "always"` continues to insert a closing bracket unconditionally by design. Quote auto-closing is unchanged.

# Manual checklist

- [x] In a JSON or JSONC document, remove an opening `{` while leaving its matching `}` later in the document, then retype `{` and verify that no duplicate `}` is inserted.
- [x] In an empty document, type `{`, `[`, and `(` and verify that each still inserts its matching closer.
- [x] Put a non-matching closer after the cursor, type an opening bracket, and verify that its matching closer is still inserted.
- [x] Verify that bracket characters inside strings, comments, and an embedded-language region do not suppress normal auto-closing.
- [x] Repeat the unmatched-closer scenario with multiple cursors and verify the shared auto-closing behavior described above.
- [x] Set `editor.autoClosingBrackets` to `always` and verify that typing an opener always inserts its closer.

## 🤖 SDK/CLI bump-fix status — cycle 4

**Pair under test:** SDK `1.0.13-preview.2` · CLI `1.0.82-0`

### What broke (authoritative: product build 468852)
Agent Host E2E — Copilot: *"plugin MCP sampling cancellation returns to the model"* (`mcpPluginSuite.ts`) failed. The test drives a runtime-hosted MCP server (launched via `.mcp.json`) whose tool calls `server.createMessage` (sampling). With no sampling UI the request must auto-cancel and return the canned `MCP_SAMPLE:The user cancelled the request.` text; instead the observed tool result was `MCP error -32001: Request timed out` — the sampling `createMessage` hung.

### Root cause (mechanism, not symptom)
The bumped **`@github/copilot` 1.0.82 runtime** now registers a per-session **host wildcard event forwarder** (`sdkServerHost.ts` `setupSessionEventForwarding` → `session.on("*")`), which calls `sessionRegisterEventHandlerSubscription` with a Host owner token, registering a Host-target **wildcard** `event_handler_subscription`. The runtime's `has_event_listener("sampling.requested")` (`registry.rs`) returns true on any Host-target wildcard subscription, so `dispatch_sampling` (`interaction.rs`) now routes the MCP server's sampling to the host and awaits it instead of firing `cancelled_sampling_response()`. VS Code has no sampling handler for runtime-hosted servers, so nothing resolves it → hang → `-32001`. Pre-bump (CLI 1.0.81-0) the wildcard forwarder was not counted, so the canned cancel fired and the test passed. This is an **intentional runtime contract change**, not a VS Code regression.

### SDK+CLI correlation / compatibility
The failing test is named directly in the build digest for **this exact signed pair** (SDK `1.0.13-preview.2` + CLI `1.0.82-0`). The mechanism is confirmed in the pinned CLI runtime source (`$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/copilot-agent-runtime`) and the SDK doc (`rpc.d.ts`: long-poll SDK clients are not auto-listeners; hosts must explicitly resolve pending sampling). The Slack canary (SDK `1.0.12-canary.55` + CLI `1.0.82-canary.58`) shares the CLI base only and was treated as hypothesis. No SDK bump needed; contract change is CLI-runtime-side.

### Fix this cycle
VS Code now explicitly **rejects pending runtime-hosted MCP sampling requests** (it has no sampling UI for them), so the runtime returns the canned cancellation instead of hanging:
- `copilotSessionWrapper.ts` — add typed `onSamplingRequested` getter (`_sdkEvent('sampling.requested')`), mirroring `onPermissionRequested`.
- `copilotAgentSession.ts` — subscribe in `_subscribeToEvents()` and call `session.rpc.ui.handlePendingSampling({ requestId })` with `response` omitted (= reject/cancel), which yields `cancelled_sampling_response()` → the asserted `The user cancelled the request.` text.

**No committed Agent Host fixtures (`*.traffic.ahp.yaml`) were regenerated or edited; no version pins/lockfiles/build paths touched.** E2E cannot run locally (needs a real GitHub token); the two edited files typecheck clean (full `typecheck-client` exceeds the sandbox memory limit). The product build is the authoritative re-check.

### Product-build state
Fix pushed → product build re-dispatched automatically. Awaiting result (would re-invoke cycle 5 on failure; cycle 5 is the hard loop cap).

title: Agents - show a badge on the application icon for sessions needing attention
body:
Adds an opt-in badge on the application icon showing how many non-archived sessions in the Agents window are unread or waiting for input, so you notice a session needing you without having to keep the window in view.

### Setting

`sessions.showApplicationBadge` — **off by default**, and annotated with `experiment: { mode: 'auto' }` so it can be rolled out and rolled back through Exp (treatment `config.sessions.showApplicationBadge`) without a window reload. An explicit user value always wins over the experiment default.

The gate is real rather than cosmetic: `_enabled` is read at the top of the `_count` derived, so while disabled the contribution never subscribes to session state, never draws, and never crosses IPC.

### Platform behaviour

The implementation is asymmetric because OS support is:

- **macOS** (dock) and **Linux** (Unity launcher) render the count themselves via `app.setBadgeCount`. Nothing is drawn.
- **Windows** has no equivalent for an unpackaged Win32 app. `app.setBadgeCount` is annotated `@platform linux,darwin` and is a no-op there, and `BrowserWindow.setOverlayIcon` only accepts a bitmap. The count-rendering API (`BadgeUpdateManager`) requires MSIX package identity, which VS Code's Inno Setup installer does not have. So the renderer draws a themed overlay (using `activityBarBadge.*` colors) and hands it to the main process. This is the same approach Slack takes; new Teams gets the OS badge only because it is MSIX-packaged.

### Notes for reviewers

- The badge crosses a `ProxyChannel`, which only revives a `VSBuffer` passed as a **top-level argument** — one nested inside an object falls through to `JSON.stringify` and arrives unusable. The icon is therefore a `data:` URL string, and there is a regression test running the real `serialize`/`deserialize` pair over the payload.
- `DockBadgeManager` now owns the application-wide badge for both the transient `FocusMode.Notify` attention dot and the per-window counts, so the two can no longer overwrite each other. Counts are keyed by window id and released on window dispose, so a closed or crashed window cannot strand a phantom badge. `setApplicationBadge` sits on `IBaseWindow` alongside `setDocumentEdited`, so `nativeHostMainService` does not need to reach into `windowImpl`.

### Validation

- 4 new unit tests (count filtering, off-until-enabled, reactivity, IPC round trip) plus the existing `windowsFinder` suite — 9 passing.
- ESLint clean on all changed files, which also enforces the `vs/sessions` layering rules.
- `npm run typecheck-client` reports no errors in any touched file. Note that `node_modules/electron` is not installed in a normal worktree, so the `electron-main` files are otherwise skipped; I temporarily supplied the Electron 42 typings to get them genuinely type-checked, then removed the stub.

title: chat: summarize Agent Merge turns in the prompt timeline
body:
## Description

Agent Merge drives its repair turns with a machine-facing `<agent_merge_state>` block. The prompt timeline (the chat "mini map") previews each prompt with its first non-empty line, so every merge turn showed up in the gutter rail, ruler hover card and sticky header as a bare `<agent_merge_state>` tag.

### Changes

- **`promptTimelineModel.ts`** — previews a request with `getAgentMergeRequestLabel()`, falling back to the message text. This is the same localized summary the transcript renders in place of the state block, and the same helper `chatFindModel` and `chatAccessibilityProvider` already use. All rails derive from `PromptTimelineModel`, so one change covers the dot list, ruler, hover card, sticky header and the ticks' `ariaLabel`.

  ```ts
  private _requestPreview(item: IChatRequestViewModel): string {
      // …
      const preview = getPromptPreview(getAgentMergeRequestLabel(item) ?? messageText);
      // …
  }
  ```

- **Preview memoization** — keyed on the prompt's text, cleared with the sibling signal cache on rebind. `_recompute()` runs on every streamed token, and recognizing a merge turn means parsing its whole state block: ~29 µs for a realistic 10 KB prompt versus ~3 µs for the plain preview.

- **Test** — builds a real prompt with `buildAgentMergePrompt` and asserts the tick reads `Agent Merge, 1 comment, 1 check failing`.

### Notes for review

Two alternatives were considered and not taken:

- **Excluding merge turns from the timeline** (matching live sessions, where `isSystemInitiated` filters them out). These turns only reach the timeline in *restored* sessions, where the transcript renders them as a full raw user bubble — hiding them would leave a large visible turn with no rail entry and make the sticky header name the wrong prompt. Relabelling also degrades gracefully if a human ever pastes a state block.
- **Restoring the turn origin in `mapSessionEvents`**, which would fix the transcript too. Left alone here: it changes protocol-level state well outside this bug, and that layer deliberately avoids content sniffing.

The underlying cause is worth a separate look: `_startAgentMergePrompt` marks these turns `MessageKind.SystemNotification`, but `mapSessionEvents` rebuilds them from the SDK log as plain user turns, so the transcript's compact merge widget also stops rendering after a restore.

title: fix: compare Position-like objects via line and character
body:
`Position` and `Range` already accept `{ line, character }` literals (`isPosition` / the existing `Range, contains (no instanceof)` test). Comparisons still read `other._line` / `other._character`, which literals do not have.

That made instance and literal disagree:

- `range.contains({ line: 3, character: 0 })` was `true` while `range.contains(new Position(3, 0))` was `false` for a range that ends at `(2, 11)`.
- `Position.isBefore` / `compareTo` had the same split: the start bound in `contains` used `Position.of`, the end bound passed the duck through.

This change compares via public `line` / `character` (and uses `Position.of` for both bounds in `contains`). Tests cover after-end / before-start literals and `compareTo` on a literal.

Not in this PR: `new Position(NaN, 0)` still does not throw (`line < 0` is false for NaN).

title: Allow reverting from Agent Host to Local chat via settings (Fixes #332129, #333154)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #332129
Fixes #333154

Make the remembered session type resolution logic symmetric with respect to Copilot harness settings in `getDefaultNewChatSessionTypeAndReasonFromServices`.

### Background & Problem

In PR #330068, `preferCopilotHarness: true` was made to consistently override a remembered `localChatSessionType`.
However, once `AgentHostCopilot` was recorded in profile storage (`chat.userSelectedSessionType`), the condition:
```typescript
if (remembered && (remembered !== localChatSessionType || !preferCopilotHarness))
```
caused `remembered` to unconditionally win whenever `remembered === SessionType.AgentHostCopilot`, because `remembered !== localChatSessionType` was always `true`.

Consequently, even when a user explicitly disabled the Copilot harness in settings:
- `"chat.editor.preferCopilotHarness": false`
- `"chat.defaultToCopilotHarness": false`
- `"chat.editor.localAgent.enabled": true`

every new chat remained permanently routed to `agent-host-copilotcli`. This locked users out of third-party language models registered in the Extension Host unless they manually deleted the internal SQLite row in `state.vscdb`.

### Proposed Change

1. Symmetrically allow a remembered `SessionType.AgentHostCopilot` to yield to `localChatSessionType` when Copilot harness is neither preferred nor default (`!preferCopilotHarness && !copilotHarnessDefault && localAgentEnabled`).
2. Continue to preserve explicit non-Copilot agent selections (`AgentHostClaude`, `AgentHostCodex`) as introduced in #330068.
3. Added unit tests in `constants.test.ts` to verify:
   - Remembered Copilot yields to Local when Copilot harness is neither default nor preferred.
   - Remembered Claude/Codex sessions remain strictly preserved when Copilot harness is disabled.

## Validation

- Added unit tests in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/constants.test.ts`:
  - `remembered Copilot session yields to Local when Copilot harness is neither default nor preferred`
  - `remembered Claude session is preserved even when Copilot harness is disabled`

title: chat: report managedSandboxEnforced in chat request telemetry
body:
Reports `managedSandboxEnforced` on the `interactiveSessionProviderInvoked` event, and documents the dependency in the existing setting comments.

### Why

The harness used for a chat request is not fully determined by the three settings the event already reports. Both harness predicates OR in the managed sandbox floor:

```ts
function isCopilotHarnessDefault(configurationService, managedSandboxEnforced = false) {
    return configurationService.getValue(ChatConfiguration.DefaultToCopilotHarness) === true
        || managedSandboxEnforced;
}
```

…and `isEditorLocalAgentEnabled` returns `false` outright when it is set.

So an enterprise on the managed sandbox floor runs on the Copilot harness while reporting `settingDefaultToCopilotHarness: false` and `settingPreferCopilotHarness: false`. In telemetry that is currently **indistinguishable** from a default that resolved incorrectly.

This came out of investigating the `Computed default` bucket on the [Copilot Harness Rollout](https://dataexplorer.azure.com/dashboards/f63cf8e6-5c88-4528-ba39-a3361f425301) dashboard, where separating "we mis-resolved" from "something else forced this" turned out to be the central difficulty. Today's cohort is unaffected (no sandbox-enforced tenants are enrolled yet), so this is a gap to close before it distorts the data rather than a live bug.

### Notes for review

- `managedSandboxEnforced` is deliberately **not** prefixed `setting`, because it is not a configuration setting — it is a separate input to the harness decision, read from `IAgentHostEnablementService`.
- The three existing comments keep the wording "the effective value of …", which is accurate: `getValue()` returns the consolidated value across default/user/workspace/folder/policy layers. They only gain a sentence noting that the harness decision has this additional input.
- `IAgentHostEnablementService` is newly injected into `ChatService`. `workbench/contrib/chat/common/` already imports from `platform/agentHost/common/` elsewhere, and `valid-layers-check` passes.

### Validation

- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passes
- `./scripts/test.sh --grep "ChatService"` — 94 passing

The unit-test change is required, not incidental: the suite did not stub the newly injected service and failed with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'managedSandboxEnforced')` until the stub was added.

title: Add aggregated fetcher fallback telemetry
body:
## Summary

Adds rate-limited telemetry for fallback sweeps where every fetcher fails or a terminal HTTP response stops further retries. Also adopts the terminal-response behavior from #331821 for HTTP 429, 502, and 503.

<details>
<summary>Session Context</summary>

Key decisions from the development session:

- **Opportunistic aggregation**: Keep module-level message-to-count maps and flush them when a fallback-enabled request enters after 15 minutes, avoiding a reporter class, timer, and FetcherService lifecycle changes.
- **Separate outcomes**: Emit `fetcherAllFailed` only when every fetcher is exhausted, and `fetcherTerminalResponse` when a terminal response stops the sweep.
- **Full terminal sweep context**: The terminal-response event includes preceding transport or parse failures as well as the terminal response because those failures would not appear in the all-failed event.
- **Bounded malformed-response reason**: Record successful responses with malformed JSON as `invalid-json` instead of a misleading 200 status message.
- **Terminal response behavior**: HTTP 429, 502, and 503 return immediately. If reached on a fallback fetcher after an earlier failure, that working fetcher is promoted while earlier bad-fetcher state is preserved.

</details>

## Changes

- Aggregate all-fetcher failures and terminal-response sweeps over 15-minute intervals.
- Preserve individual failure-message counts in each telemetry payload.
- Stop fallback retries for terminal HTTP responses.
- Add focused coverage for timing, aggregation, active fetcher variants, fallback promotion, and invalid JSON.

## Validation

- Focused `fetcherFallback.spec.ts` suite: 9 tests passed.
- Editor diagnostics and `git diff --check`: clean.

title: agentHost: let an Agents Window claim an existing external session
body:
### What this does

A controller that already owns a remote Agent Host session can launch an Agents Window and
have it *join* that exact session as an additional active client, so the window contributes
its tool inventory — notably the integrated browser's agentic tools such as `readPage` — to a
session the controller keeps driving.

Today there is no way to do this. A window can open a session it created, but nothing lets an
outside owner hand an existing session to a window without the window taking over turn control
or creating a session of its own.

### How it works

1. A private, unlisted launch argument `--agent-session-claim-hash` carries a hex SHA-256
   **commitment**. It has no `cat`, so it never appears in `--help`, and it is not a secret:
   argv is world-readable, and a commitment is useless without its pre-image.
2. A hidden command, `workbench.action.agentHost.claimExternalSession`, is registered **only**
   in a window launched with an unspent commitment. It has no `metadata`, so it is absent from
   the Command Palette, and it is contributed to no menu.
3. A bridge extension invokes it with the pre-image, which pins the session type, session URI,
   and bridge identity alongside a nonce. Fields are hashed with a netstring-style canonical
   encoding (`<len>:<value>`), so no two distinct claims encode to the same bytes.
4. The handler joins the existing session, makes it active on the ordinary
   `ISessionsService.openSession` path a sidebar click takes, and publishes the window's tool
   inventory as an active client, holding a refcount.

### Security boundary

* The command does not exist in an ordinary window. Without a valid commitment the
  contribution returns before registering anything.
* The claim is **one-use**. The in-memory commitment is cleared and a spent marker is written
  to storage *before* the request is parsed or validated, so a malformed or non-matching
  request still burns it. A window reload replays the same argv, so the marker — not the
  argument — is what enforces this.
* The request is validated strictly: exactly the expected keys, each non-empty printable
  ASCII, and a session URI that must re-serialize to itself. ASCII is required so the length
  prefix is byte-exact for a controller written in another language.
* No secret reaches argv, storage, logs, or error messages.

### Behaviour

The claim joins an **existing** session and nothing else. It creates no session, materializes
none, sends no prompt, turn, or authentication frame, and writes no draft or pending message.
The controller remains the sole owner of turns, policy, and transcript. Releasing the claim
publishes the removal only when it is the last holder, so a chat opened on the same session
keeps working.

### Non-goals

* No user-facing feature: no setting, no command palette entry, no menu, no UI.
* No public API and no new proposed API.
* No UI automation, and no change to how ordinary editors or sessions behave.
* Not enabled in any released build; the external client that drives it is gated and refuses
  unless the build it runs actually carries this path.

### Validation

Typecheck, transpile, layers check, and ESLint are clean on this branch. 128 unit tests cover
the commitment and validation rules, the command surface, target readiness, the claim
lifecycle, and two regressions: that the first published inventory contains tools registered
during activation rather than waiting for the tools-registry debounce, and that a displaced
chat releases its active-client hold.

End to end, a canary build of this exact product change was driven twice against a real
session. Both runs claimed the exact existing session, published all ten `vscode-browser`
tools in the first settled inventory, routed `openBrowserPage` and `readPage` to the window,
returned a page sentinel through the tool result and the assistant response, ran exactly one
evaluated turn with no window-originated turn, and detached cleanly leaving the host running.

That evidence was collected on an earlier base. The change here is byte-identical in its added
and removed lines; main has since changed only turn-completion handling in the same file,
which the tests above cover.

title: fix: use fuzzy match for internal clearEditorHistory automation command (build fix for vscode-engineering#3718)
body:
## Build failure

The `Data Loss (stable -> insiders)` smoke tests (`Run smoke tests (Electron)`) failed identically on Windows, Linux, and macOS with:

```
QuickAccess.runCommand(commandId: workbench.action.clearEditorHistoryWithoutConfirm, match: exactCommandId) failed to find command.
  at QuickAccess.runCommand (test/automation/out/quickaccess.js)
  at async QuickAccess.openFileQuickAccessAndWait
  at async QuickAccess.openFile
```

The failure originates from `QuickAccess.openFile` -> `openFileQuickAccessAndWait`, which internally clears editor history before opening a file. On macOS this also cascaded into a `Language Features > verifies quick outline (js)` timeout via the same broken quick-access path.

## Root cause

`test/automation/src/quickaccess.ts` `runCommand` gained a `CommandMatchMode` option whose default is now `exactCommandId`. That mode matches the focused quick-pick entry via `element.id === commandId`, where `element.id` is read from the new `data-quick-input-id` DOM attribute set by `QuickPickItemElementRenderer.renderElement` in `src/vs/platform/quickinput/browser/quickInputList.ts`.

The `Data Loss (stable -> insiders)` tests first launch an **older stable build** of VS Code. `openFileQuickAccessAndWait` runs `clearEditorHistoryWithoutConfirm` against that stable build, which does **not** emit the `data-quick-input-id` attribute. As a result `element.id` is `undefined`, the `exactCommandId` match never succeeds, and the command is reported as not found after all retries.

Several call sites were updated to `match: 'exactLabel'` for backward compatibility, but this internal call inside `openFileQuickAccessAndWait` was not, so it silently regressed to the new default `exactCommandId` against builds that cannot satisfy it.

## How the fix works

The internal call passes a command **id** (`workbench.action.clearEditorHistoryWithoutConfirm`) as the palette query. The command-palette filter already narrows results to exactly that command when the `>`-prefixed id is typed, so a strict id/label DOM match is unnecessary here. Switching this single call to `match: 'fuzzy'` restores the pre-regression behavior — accepting the focused entry once the palette has filtered down — and works against both stable and insiders builds regardless of whether the new `data-quick-input-id` metadata is present.

Only the internal history-clearing helper is changed; other call sites that always run against the current build continue to use `exactCommandId`/`exactLabel` as intended. No product code or telemetry is affected.

## Rollback evaluation

Recommendation: **Do not roll back.**

Public culprit: commit `e2b48f58` — PR microsoft/vscode#332892 ("Launch Skill: Quick Pick should expose item IDs for automation").

Rationale: The culprit change is broadly useful (it adds automation-facing item ids) and touches many files; a full revert would discard that value. The regression is a single missed call site in test automation, and this fix-forward is bounded, low-risk, and restores green without cross-repository work. title: debug: work around frozen renderer when launching from Run and Debug
body:
> **Authored by GitHub Copilot** on behalf of @jruales. Draft — temporary workaround, not a product change.

## Problem

Launching the workbench with the **VS Code** or **Renderer and Main processes** compound can leave the window painted but completely unresponsive: nothing is clickable, the keyboard does nothing, the command palette opens but neither responds nor dismisses, and the extension host never finishes starting.

The renderer is stuck in the debugger's *waiting-for-debugger* state. Confirmed on a stuck window:

- `Runtime.evaluate` of synchronous code succeeds
- `setTimeout` and `requestAnimationFrame` never fire; event handlers never run
- `Debugger.resume` returns `Can only perform operation while paused`
- `Runtime.runIfWaitingForDebugger` immediately restores the window

## Cause (upstream, in js-debug)

`Inspector.workerScriptLoaded` — a Blink event fired when a web worker finishes evaluating — can arrive for a session js-debug hasn't registered yet, because `targetCreated` is queued through `enqueueLifecycleFn` while workers such as `editorWorkerService` start immediately. js-debug throws on unknown session ids, the throw escapes `EventEmitter.fire` leaving its delivery queue populated, and every later `fire` then returns without dispatching. That permanently kills the CDP message pump, so `Runtime.runIfWaitingForDebugger` is never sent.

```
Error: Unknown session id: B9878282765DBAAB165E4A5851627507 while processing: Inspector.workerScriptLoaded
    at ut._onMessage (.../ms-vscode.js-debug/src/extension.js:58:8166)
    at U.fire        (.../ms-vscode.js-debug/src/extension.js:39:11654)
```

Reported as microsoft/vscode-js-debug#2401, fix proposed in microsoft/vscode-js-debug#2402.

## This change

Adds a hidden `Resume Stuck Renderer` configuration to the two affected compounds. It waits 8s so js-debug can attach normally, then resumes the renderer only if its event loop never turns. It is inert on a healthy renderer.

## Validation

Root cause and fix confirmed by a controlled A/B: js-debug built with and without the upstream fix, loaded into a real VS Code Insiders window via `--extensionDevelopmentPath`, same machine, repo, profile and launch compound.

| js-debug build | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Unpatched | Workbench freezes. Reproduced repeatedly. |
| Patched | Works every time. |

Not environment-specific: it also reproduces with a completely empty Code OSS profile, and `.build/electron` matches the pinned `42.8.1`. It is timing-sensitive, so it may not reproduce on every machine.

The workaround itself was verified to stay silent against a healthy renderer and to log `Resumed renderer that was waiting for the debugger` against a deliberately stalled one.

## Notes for reviewers

- Draft, and intended to be **reverted** once microsoft/vscode-js-debug#2402 ships in the bundled js-debug.
- Written as `.ts` rather than `.js` to satisfy the pre-commit check; Node runs it directly via type stripping.
- Port `9222` is hardcoded to match `Launch VS Code Internal`.

title: Fix sign-in dead-end in installed web apps (PWA)
body: Signing in from an installed web app (PWA) dead-ends: tapping **Continue with GitHub** shows *"The browser blocked opening a new tab or window"*, no sign-in window appears, and the **Retry** button is covered by the "Signing in…" modal so it cannot even be pressed. ## Cause Browsers only allow `window.open` while a click's user activation is still live. Chat sign-in does a lot between the click and the open — shows a dialog, activates the authentication extension, requests an authorization URL over the network — so by the time it opens anything the gesture has expired and the window is refused. In a browser tab this is survivable: the prompt appears and **Retry** works, because Retry runs inside a fresh click. In an installed web app there is no tab to fall back to, and the prompt is unreachable, so sign-in cannot be completed at all. Measured on an iPhone PWA, `window.open()` succeeds inside a real tap and is refused outside one: | call | inside a tap | outside a tap | | --- | --- | --- | | `window.open()` | ✅ | ❌ | | `window.open(url, '_blank')` | ✅ | ❌ | | `window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener')` | ❌ | ❌ | (`noopener` is refused even inside a tap — an installed app has no independent browsing context to hand it to.) ## Change Claim the window synchronously on the click, then navigate that reserved window once the URL is known. - `reserveWindowForExternalOpen()` opens the window during the click and shows a short placeholder, since the window is visible immediately but the URL may be a second or more away. - `windowOpenWithSuccess()` consumes the reservation if there is one, and otherwise behaves exactly as before. - `releaseReservedWindowForExternalOpen()` closes the window when setup ends without using it. `close()` is not always honoured — an in-app browser view can ignore it — so if the window survives it is given a short explanation rather than left blank on top of the app. Gated on `isStandalone() || isSafari`: installed apps fail this way in whichever browser installed them, and Safari blocks the popup in tabs too. Everywhere else popups still work after the gesture, so nothing is reserved and behaviour is unchanged. ## Testing - Verified on an iPhone PWA that the sign-in window now opens on tap with no warning dialog. Full end-to-end sign-in still needs a host where the `github-authentication` extension loads; a local tunnel cannot exercise it. - Placeholder rendering, navigation of the reserved window, `close()`, and the refuses-to-close fallback verified in WebKit. - `tsc` and `eslint` clean. Draft while the end-to-end run on insiders is pending.

auto_merge.commit_title: Fix sign-in dead-end in installed web apps (PWA) (#333084)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* Reserve the sign-in window during the user gesture

Browsers only allow `window.open` while a click's user activation is still
live. Chat sign-in shows a dialog, activates an extension and fetches an
authorization URL first, so by the time it opens anything the gesture has
expired and Safari refuses the window.

In a browser tab this surfaces as a "browser blocked opening a new tab"
prompt whose Retry works, because Retry runs inside a fresh click. In an
installed web app (PWA) on iOS there is no tab to fall back to and the
prompt is covered by the "Signing in..." modal, so sign-in dead-ends with
no way forward.

Claim the window synchronously on the click instead, and let
`windowOpenWithSuccess` navigate that reserved window once the URL is
known. Gated to Safari, so other browsers are unaffected. The reservation
is released when setup ends without using it, so a cancelled or failed
sign-in does not leave a blank window over the app.

Verified on an iPhone PWA that `window.open()` succeeds inside a real tap
and is refused outside one.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Cover installed web apps in any browser, not just Safari

The reservation was gated on Safari, but the failure is a property of
installed web apps rather than of one browser: an app installed through
Edge or Chrome has no tab to fall back to either, and sign-in dead-ends
there the same way.

Gate on `isStandalone() || isSafari` instead, and route standalone
through the open-then-navigate path so a reserved window is actually
consumed. Browser tabs outside Safari are unaffected.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Do not leave a blank window behind when sign-in does not complete

The reserved window is released when setup ends without using it, but
`close()` is not always honoured — an in-app browser view on iOS can
ignore it — which would leave a blank window covering the app. That is
worse than the popup block this change exists to fix.

Show a short explanation in the window when it refuses to close, and
render the placeholder via `textContent` on a document that follows the
system colour scheme, so it neither flashes white nor can inject markup.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Address review feedback

- Reserve only for strategies that actually enter provider authentication.
  `DefaultSetup` can install and sign up without any browser round trip for
  an already signed-in user, so reserving for it left a window covering the
  app for the whole of setup.
- Open from the window the click happened in. User activation belongs to
  that window, so a dialog shown in an auxiliary window could still be
  blocked when opening from `mainWindow`.
- Give the placeholder document a title, so screen readers and window
  switchers do not announce it as `about:blank`.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Trim comments to the non-obvious parts

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Narrow the popup workaround to installed mobile apps

`isStandalone()` also matches desktop installed apps, including a
self-hosted VS Code installed from the server's manifest. Those get real
windows and can open popups after the gesture, so they were being pulled
onto the open-then-navigate path — and its manual `opener` nulling — for
no benefit.

Add `isMobileStandalone()` and gate on that instead, keeping the
workaround where a blocked popup is actually unrecoverable.

title: agentHost: avoid duplicate subagents on reconnect
body:
- Reconnecting to an active Agent Host turn used two independent progress producers: activeTurnToProgress created a one-shot snapshot while _observeTurn replayed and continued observing the same response parts. This made correctness depend on manually keeping snapshot adoption, emitted text lengths, and response-part offsets synchronized.

- A settled subagent tool exposed the weakness because the snapshot rendered a serialized parent invocation, while the live observer still needed to run to attach the child chat and forward its activity. That observer could emit a second live parent invocation, leaving the serialized snapshot without live metadata or navigation while the second card worked normally.

- Make the reactive turn observer the only reconnect progress producer. Its synchronous first pass already replays accumulated response parts before the session is returned, and subsequent updates now mutate the same live invocation instead of competing with a disconnected snapshot.

- Preserve Restore Checkpoint behavior when the observer synchronously replays file edits before the ChatModel exists. Queue those edits per session and flush them into AgentHostSnapshotController when the matching model is created.

- Add reconnect regressions for completed subagent tools, completed file edits, settled tools followed by streaming markdown, streaming tool transitions, and owned client tools. These assert that reconnect renders exactly one invocation while retaining child-chat updates and checkpoint data.

title: sessions: govern single-pane bottom panel at workbench level, remember its view per session
body:
## What

In the **single-pane** layout, the bottom panel is now handled like the side pane:

- **Visibility** is governed at the **workbench level** (not per session) and persisted across reloads.
- **Which view** the panel shows is remembered **per session** and restored on session switch or when the panel is revealed — never forcing the panel open (restoring a view while the panel is hidden would reveal it).
- A session with **no remembered view defaults to the Terminal**.

The **classic** layout is unchanged: it still remembers panel *visibility* per session and lets the view follow the global last-active.

## How

A single `_isPanelVisibilityPerSession` gate on `BaseLayoutController` drives both scopes — they are inverse, never both:

- `true` (classic): panel **visibility** is per session (`[B1]`).
- `false` (single-pane): panel **view** is per session instead (`[B6]`), persisted as `panelViewContainerId`.

`_syncPanelView` restores the remembered view (falling back to `TERMINAL_VIEW_ID`) only while the panel is already visible, via the session-switch autorun and a `PANEL_PART` visibility listener. Workbench-level panel visibility is saved/restored in `workbench.ts` alongside the other parts, gated on the single-pane layout.

## Notes for reviewers

- The single-pane controller overrides just the one `_isPanelVisibilityPerSession` flag; everything else derives from it.
- Spec updated in `baseSessionLayoutController.md` (`[B1]`, `[B6]`).
- Tests: added `[B6]` coverage (restore on switch/reveal, does not force the panel open while hidden, persistence + reload, Terminal default) and `[B1]` coverage for the workbench-level single-pane behavior. Full `BaseLayoutController` suite passes; typecheck and hygiene clean.

title: agent host: expose MCP support assessment
body:
## Summary

- Adds an internal, refcounted support scope that VS Code consumers can query before or during a Copilot CLI Agent Host session.
- Makes every known MCP server's source, client enablement, workspace applicability, delivery owner, compatibility, and reason codes available in one reactive snapshot.
- Includes installed servers disabled before runtime registration and waits for the initial installed-server inventory before resolving the first snapshot.
- Reports when discovery, MCP access, or customization policy limits coverage.
- Integrates the support assessment with customization migration as a binary supported/not-supported result, including discovery and coverage metadata.
- Reuses the same delivery resolver as the real forwarding path so reported support stays aligned with Agent Host behavior.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Consumer[VS Code consumer] --> Scope[MCP support scope]
    Inventory[MCP runtime and installed inventory] --> Scope
    Scope --> Snapshot[Reactive support snapshot]
    Snapshot --> Migration[Customization migration]
    Snapshot --> Decision[Other presentation or routing decisions]
```

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

Workbench consumers could inspect servers already published by an active Agent Host session, but they had no client-side query that answered which configured servers were known before session creation, how each server would reach the host, or why a configuration could not be represented. Servers disabled by MCP access could also be absent from the runtime registry entirely.

The customization migration service also had no way to report whether discovered MCP servers were compatible with an Agent Host harness.

### Support assessment

`IAgentHostActiveClientService.acquireMcpServerSupportScope(sessionType, roots)` returns a shared scope for Copilot CLI harnesses. A one-shot consumer waits for `whenResolved()`, reads `scope.support.get()`, and disposes the scope; reactive consumers can observe `support` while retaining the same disposable reference.

The snapshot exposes per-server source metadata, enablement, applicability to the requested working directories, delivery path, compatibility, and structured incompatibility reasons. It also exposes lazy-discovery completeness and coverage flags for MCP access and strict customization policy.

The assessment merges the runtime MCP registry with the installed-server inventory so access-disabled configurations remain visible. `IMcpWorkbenchService.whenInitialLocalMcpServersLoaded` prevents the first support snapshot from treating the asynchronously populated installed inventory as empty. Initial query failures are logged and settle readiness so later refreshes do not repeatedly reject.

Collection provenance distinguishes VS Code user, remote, workspace, workspace-folder, root `.mcp.json`, extension, plugin, and externally discovered sources such as Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Windsurf.

### Customization migration integration

`CustomizationMigrationType.McpServers` adds a discriminated MCP migration result. The browser-layer implementation acquires the support scope, waits for resolution, filters servers outside the requested roots, maps exact `supported` compatibility to `supported: true`, and collapses partial, unsupported, and unknown compatibility to `false`.

The migration result also carries `discoveryComplete` and snapshot-wide MCP access/customization policy coverage flags. Enablement remains independent from compatibility.

The concrete migration service moved from `chat/common` to `chat/browser/aiCustomization` because it now injects the browser-layer `IAgentHostActiveClientService`. The shared service contract and DTOs remain in `chat/common`.

### Behavior and constraints

- The utility is an internal workbench API, not an extension API.
- `undefined` roots preserve unknown workspace applicability; an empty root array means there is no workspace.
- Enablement, applicability, delivery, and compatibility are independent. A disabled server can still have a supported configuration.
- Delivery distinguishes client-forwarded, runtime-discovered, plugin-provided, provider-built-in, not-delivered, and unknown cases.
- Partial and unsupported results explain ignored environment files, sandbox settings, development mode, OAuth client configuration, unresolved variables, interaction requirements, unsupported source locations, and unloaded definitions.
- Support scopes are created only when requested, shared by normalized session type and roots, refreshed when their inputs change, and disposed after their final consumer releases them.

### Review context

The main review boundary is consistency between support reporting and actual MCP forwarding. Both paths share delivery resolution, while enablement and disabled installed-server synthesis remain reporting-only so regular forwarding does not pay for diagnostic state.

The customization migration integration intentionally exposes only binary compatibility for now while preserving completeness and coverage metadata needed to interpret that result.

</details>
